claims.claim_text_verbatim: We introduce Universal Textual Teaching (UTT), a parameter-update-free framework that distills observed Teacher-Student knowledge gaps into a textual, interpretable, and reusable natural-language artifact called Primer.
claims.claim_summary: UTT distills Teacher-Student knowledge gaps into an interpretable natural-language Primer without parameter updates.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Empirically, on the challenging math (Omni-MATH-2) and code generation (KernelBench) tasks, extensive results confirm the effectiveness of the method: UTT remarkably raises the Student’s accuracy from 9.4% to 48.6% and Fast1 accuracy from 9% to 35% on KernelBench, while increasing mathematical reasoning accuracy from 27.6% to 51.7%.
claims.claim_summary: UTT significantly improves Student accuracy and Fast1 on KernelBench and Omni-MATH-2.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: UTT also performs better than representative prompt engineering and parameter-based KD methods.
claims.claim_summary: UTT outperforms representative prompt engineering and parameter-updating knowledge distillation methods.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Of note, UTT is shown to be generalizable across different Teachers and Students: a Primer synthesized for one Teacher-Student pair can generalize to other Students that do not participate in the synthesis.
claims.claim_summary: Primers synthesized for one Teacher-Student pair generalize to other Students without resynthesis.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Relying solely on interactions among LLMs, the process requires no model training or parameter updates and supports both open-source and API-only commercial models.
claims.claim_summary: UTT requires no model training or parameter updates and supports API-only commercial models.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Empirically, across various Teacher-Student configurations in mathematical reasoning and code generation, the synthesized Primers consistently improve their source Students and remain effective when transferred to other Students without resynthesis, demonstrating both effectiveness and cross-model reusability.
claims.claim_summary: Primers consistently improve source Students and remain effective when transferred across models.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Relative to the unprimed Student baselines, UTT improves KernelBench accuracy from 9.4% to 48.6%, Fast1 from 9% to 35%, and mathematical reasoning accuracy from 27.6% to 51.7%.
claims.claim_summary: UTT boosts KernelBench accuracy, Fast1, and math accuracy over unprimed baselines.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Across the evaluated settings, UTT also outperforms representative prompt engineering and parameter-updating knowledge distillation methods.
claims.claim_summary: UTT outperforms prompt engineering and parameter-updating KD across evaluated settings.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: We formulate LLM distillation as representing the Teacher-Student knowledge gap in natural language rather than encoding it in a specific Student’s parameters, making the distilled knowledge interpretable and reusable across models.
claims.claim_summary: Formulating KD in natural language makes distilled knowledge interpretable and reusable across models.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: UTT identifies knowledge gaps through paired evaluation and iteratively synthesizes a deployable global Primer from Student attempts, Prompter feedback, and Teacher demonstrations, without updating any model parameters.
claims.claim_summary: UTT synthesizes a deployable global Primer without updating any model parameters.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Across math and code tasks, UTT demonstrates effectiveness and transferability, with Primers transferable across models without resynthesis.
claims.claim_summary: UTT demonstrates effectiveness and cross-model transferability without resynthesis across tasks.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Notably, the resulting Primer can improve the performance of the source Student and other Students that are not involved in creating the Primer.
claims.claim_summary: Primers improve performance for both source Students and uninvolved target Students.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: For the target Student Qwen3.6-27B, Primers synthesized from the Teacher-Student pairs (shown at the bottom of the figure) consistently improve accuracy.
claims.claim_summary: Primers synthesized from Teacher-Student pairs consistently improve Qwen3.6-27B accuracy.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Even when Qwen3.6-27B does not participate in the Primer synthesis, the absolute accuracy gains reach 41.8% and 31.5% (see the rightmost column) on KernelBench and Omni-MATH-2, respectively.
claims.claim_summary: Transferring Primers to Qwen3.6-27B yields up to 41.8% and 31.5% accuracy gains.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The Primer yields substantial gains of 39.2, 26, and 24.1 percentage points over the Student baseline on KernelBench accuracy, Fast1, and Math accuracy, respectively, improving the corresponding scores from 9.4% to 48.6%, 9% to 35%, and 27.6% to 51.7%.
claims.claim_summary: Pro->Flash Primer increases KernelBench accuracy, Fast1, and Math accuracy substantially.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Keeping Pro as the Teacher, we further synthesize a new Primer for Qwen, which achieves 50.0%, 32%, and 62.4% on the same metrics.
claims.claim_summary: Pro->Qwen Primer achieves 50.0% KernelBench accuracy, 32% Fast1, and 62.4% Math accuracy.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The Flash-derived Primer improves Qwen by 32.0, 25, and 25.8 percentage points in KernelBench accuracy, Fast1, and Math accuracy, respectively.
claims.claim_summary: Flash-derived Primer improves Qwen by 32.0, 25, and 25.8 points across metrics.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The Qwen-derived Primer improves Flash by 34.4, 21, and 16.1 percentage points on the same metrics.
claims.claim_summary: Qwen-derived Primer improves Flash by 34.4, 21, and 16.1 points across metrics.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: These results show that knowledge distilled through interactions with one Student can transfer to another Student without resynthesizing the Primer.
claims.claim_summary: Knowledge distilled with one Student transfers to another Student without resynthesizing.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: It improves Flash by 38.8, 30, and 19.0 percentage points on the three metrics, demonstrating that UTT remains effective with different Teachers.
claims.claim_summary: Opus->Flash Primer improves Flash by 38.8, 30, and 19.0 percentage points.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Finally, applying this Primer unchanged to Qwen yields 51.0% KernelBench accuracy, 22% Fast1, and 65.8% Math accuracy.
claims.claim_summary: Applying the Opus-Flash Primer to Qwen reaches 51.0% accuracy and 65.8% Math accuracy.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: On the distillation training set, Pro→Flash accuracy on KernelBench increases from 6.7% to 65.2%, indicating that the synthesized Primer effectively improves Student performance on knowledge-gap samples.
claims.claim_summary: Pro->Flash accuracy on KernelBench distillation training increases from 6.7% to 65.2%.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: On the distillation test set, Pro→Qwen accuracy on the math task increases from 9.7% to 64.8%.
claims.claim_summary: Pro->Qwen math accuracy on the distillation test set rises from 9.7% to 64.8%.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: These results show that knowledge distilled into text can generalize to unseen problems, with benefits extending beyond the samples used for synthesis.
claims.claim_summary: Textually distilled knowledge generalizes to unseen problems beyond synthesis samples.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: On the retention subset, the three KernelBench configurations show no decline in accuracy; instead, they improve from 34.0% to 74.0%, 27.0% to 81.0%, and 37.1% to 78.6%, respectively.
claims.claim_summary: Retention accuracy on KernelBench improves across all three configurations without declining.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: This indicates that the Primer largely preserves the Student’s existing capabilities while improving performance on knowledge-gap samples.
claims.claim_summary: The Primer largely preserves existing capabilities while boosting performance on knowledge gaps.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: This shows that the Primer can help the Student solve some problems that neither the Teacher nor the Student solved during baseline evaluation, extending the observed capability frontier.
claims.claim_summary: Primers help Students solve problems neither Teacher nor Student solved originally.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: UTT performs best across all six combinations, with consistent gains across tasks and target models.
claims.claim_summary: UTT outperforms prompt engineering methods across all six evaluated combinations.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: With Student parameters fixed, UTT exceeds the strongest baseline by 7.2, 8.2, and 4 percentage points on Omni-MATH-2 accuracy, KernelBench accuracy, and Fast1, respectively.
claims.claim_summary: UTT beats the best parameter-updating KD baseline across all evaluated metrics.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: On the challenging math and code generation tasks (Omni-MATH-2 and KernelBench), UTT substantially improves the Student’s performance across various Teacher-Student settings.
claims.claim_summary: UTT substantially improves Student performance across various Teacher-Student settings.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Compared with knowledge implicitly encoded in model parameters, the Primer is interpretable and not tied to particular model weights, enabling direct transfer to other models.
claims.claim_summary: The Primer is interpretable, independent of weights, and directly transferable to other models.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: These results suggest that text can serve as a universal medium for knowledge transfer among different LLMs for complex tasks.
claims.claim_summary: These results suggest that text can serve as a universal medium for knowledge transfer among different LLMs for complex tasks.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: To this end, this paper presents Universal Textual Teaching (UTT), a parameter-update-free framework that distills model knowledge into a natural-language artifact called Primer1 through multi-role teaching interactions (Figure 1).
claims.claim_summary: To this end, this paper presents Universal Textual Teaching (UTT), a parameter-update-free framework that distills model knowledge into a natural-language artifact called Primer1 through multi-role teaching interactions (Figure 1).

claims.claim_text_verbatim: UTT retains the objective of knowledge distillation while explicitly representing the Teacher’s knowledge advantage over the Student as a natural-language Primer, which enhances the Student through context while keeping its parameters fixed.
claims.claim_summary: UTT retains the objective of knowledge distillation while explicitly representing the Teacher’s knowledge advantage over the Student as a natural-language Primer, which enhances the Student through context while keeping its parameters fixed.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: UTT shares with APO the use of natural-language text optimization to enhance models, but differs in its research objective and organization of supervision.
claims.claim_summary: UTT shares with APO the use of natural-language text optimization to enhance models, but differs in its research objective and organization of supervision.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: UTT pursues knowledge distillation by identifying what to transfer from the paired performance and synthesizing a global Primer from Student attempts, evaluation feedback, and validated Teacher demonstrations.
claims.claim_summary: UTT pursues knowledge distillation by identifying what to transfer from the paired performance and synthesizing a global Primer from Student attempts, evaluation feedback, and validated Teacher demonstrations.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Its distinction lies in using the observed Teacher-Student knowledge gap to guide teaching-content selection and text synthesis, while examining whether the resulting knowledge transfers to other Students without resynthesis.
claims.claim_summary: Its distinction lies in using the observed Teacher-Student knowledge gap to guide teaching-content selection and text synthesis, while examining whether the resulting knowledge transfers to other Students without resynthesis.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Experiments further validate that this language-based knowledge representation Primer not only enhances the source Student but also transfers to improve other Student models.
claims.claim_summary: Experiments further validate that this language-based knowledge representation Primer not only enhances the source Student but also transfers to improve other Student models.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: These results validate the effectiveness of UTT and demonstrate its applicability to Students from different model families.
claims.claim_summary: These results validate the effectiveness of UTT and demonstrate its applicability to Students from different model families.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: This result further demonstrates the transferability and broad applicability of UTT across diverse Teacher-Student configurations.
claims.claim_summary: This result further demonstrates the transferability and broad applicability of UTT across diverse Teacher-Student configurations.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Together, these results support effective synthesis across the evaluated model configurations without resynthesis or parameter updates.
claims.claim_summary: Together, these results support effective synthesis across the evaluated model configurations without resynthesis or parameter updates.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Although the main experiments focus on LLMs, we also preliminarily confirm transfer to multimodal LLMs in Appendix B.1.
claims.claim_summary: Although the main experiments focus on LLMs, we also preliminarily confirm transfer to multimodal LLMs in Appendix B.1.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: On Omni-MATH-2, Pro→Flash improves accuracy from 58.0% to 69.0%, while Pro→Qwen and Opus→Flash decrease accuracy by 9.2 and 14.2 percentage points, respectively, yet still retain most of their baseline performance.
claims.claim_summary: On Omni-MATH-2, Pro→Flash improves accuracy from 58.0% to 69.0%, while Pro→Qwen and Opus→Flash decrease accuracy by 9.2 and 14.2 percentage points, respectively, yet still retain most of their baseline performance.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: On the frontier subset, the primed Student achieves nonzero accuracy in five of the six configura- tions.
claims.claim_summary: On the frontier subset, the primed Student achieves nonzero accuracy in five of the six configura- tions.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The three KernelBench configurations achieve 11.7% to 18.6% accuracy, while Pro→Flash and Pro→Qwen achieve 5.3% and 30.0% on Omni-MATH-2, respectively.
claims.claim_summary: The three KernelBench configurations achieve 11.7% to 18.6% accuracy, while Pro→Flash and Pro→Qwen achieve 5.3% and 30.0% on Omni-MATH-2, respectively.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Together, these fine-grained results further support the effectiveness of UTT in four respects: syn- thesis effectiveness, generalization to unseen problems, preservation of existing capabilities, and extension of capability frontiers.
claims.claim_summary: Together, these fine-grained results further support the effectiveness of UTT in four respects: syn- thesis effectiveness, generalization to unseen problems, preservation of existing capabilities, and extension of capability frontiers.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Teacher summary improves Flash but is inconsistent on Qwen, suggesting that directly summarized Teacher knowledge may not transfer well across Students and Teacher-Student interaction is important for constructing an effective Primer.
claims.claim_summary: Teacher summary improves Flash but is inconsistent on Qwen, suggesting that directly summarized Teacher knowledge may not transfer well across Students and Teacher-Student interaction is important for constructing an effective Primer.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: These results indicate that explicit textual knowledge can yield stronger and more consistent gains across tasks.
claims.claim_summary: These results indicate that explicit textual knowledge can yield stronger and more consistent gains across tasks.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: This paper introduces Universal Textual Teaching (UTT), a parameter-update-free knowledge distil- lation method for large language models.
claims.claim_summary: This paper introduces Universal Textual Teaching (UTT), a parameter-update-free knowledge distil- lation method for large language models.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: UTT also outperforms representative prompt engineering and KD methods.
claims.claim_summary: UTT also outperforms representative prompt engineering and KD methods.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: This demonstrates that natural language can serve as a deployable knowledge carrier across models, providing a new parameter-update-free perspec- tive on knowledge distillation for large language models.
claims.claim_summary: This demonstrates that natural language can serve as a deployable knowledge carrier across models, providing a new parameter-update-free perspec- tive on knowledge distillation for large language models.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: UTT first identifies Teacher-Student knowledge gaps and then synthesizes validated teaching records into a textual Primer through multi-role LLM interactions.
claims.claim_summary: UTT first identifies Teacher-Student knowledge gaps and then synthesizes validated teaching records into a textual Primer through multi-role LLM interactions.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Table 5 shows that the Primer yields positive gains for every source and transfer Student.
claims.claim_summary: Table 5 shows that the Primer yields positive gains for every source and transfer Student.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Under Qwen3.8-Max→Qwen3.6-27B, the source Student improves from 41.5% to 76.0%, while transferring the same Primer to DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash improves its accuracy from 54.0% to 59.0%.
claims.claim_summary: Under Qwen3.8-Max→Qwen3.6-27B, the source Student improves from 41.5% to 76.0%, while transferring the same Primer to DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash improves its accuracy from 54.0% to 59.0%.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: When DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash serves as the source Student, its accuracy increases from 54.0% to 56.0%, whereas transferring the resulting Primer to Qwen3.6-27B substantially improves accuracy from 41.5% to 72.0%.
claims.claim_summary: When DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash serves as the source Student, its accuracy increases from 54.0% to 56.0%, whereas transferring the resulting Primer to Qwen3.6-27B substantially improves accuracy from 41.5% to 72.0%.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: After replacing the Teacher with Claude Opus 5, Qwen3.6-27B improves from 41.5% to 80.5%, while applying the same Primer to DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash raises its accuracy from 54.0% to 57.5%.
claims.claim_summary: After replacing the Teacher with Claude Opus 5, Qwen3.6-27B improves from 41.5% to 80.5%, while applying the same Primer to DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash raises its accuracy from 54.0% to 57.5%.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Overall, Primers synthesized by different Teachers substantially improve Qwen3.6-27B, and all cross-Student transfers retain positive gains.
claims.claim_summary: Overall, Primers synthesized by different Teachers substantially improve Qwen3.6-27B, and all cross-Student transfers retain positive gains.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: These results indicate that UTT extends to multimodal reasoning tasks requiring joint understanding of images and text, and that its textual knowledge can be reused across models.
claims.claim_summary: These results indicate that UTT extends to multimodal reasoning tasks requiring joint understanding of images and text, and that its textual knowledge can be reused across models.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The different gain magnitudes on Qwen3.6-27B and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash indicate that transfer effectiveness varies with the target Student.
claims.claim_summary: The different gain magnitudes on Qwen3.6-27B and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash indicate that transfer effectiveness varies with the target Student.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: As shown in Figure 4, accuracy generally increases with the output-token budget, while the incre- mental gains diminish at larger budgets, indicating that performance gradually approaches satura- tion.
claims.claim_summary: As shown in Figure 4, accuracy generally increases with the output-token budget, while the incre- mental gains diminish at larger budgets, indicating that performance gradually approaches satura- tion.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: UTT consistently outperforms the unprimed Student across all evaluated budgets, with a more pronounced advantage under smaller budgets.
claims.claim_summary: UTT consistently outperforms the unprimed Student across all evaluated budgets, with a more pronounced advantage under smaller budgets.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: As both curves approach saturation, UTT retains its advantage, suggesting that the Primer is particularly beneficial when the inference budget is con- strained and provides a higher effective performance ceiling within the evaluated range.
claims.claim_summary: As both curves approach saturation, UTT retains its advantage, suggesting that the Primer is particularly beneficial when the inference budget is con- strained and provides a higher effective performance ceiling within the evaluated range.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: As shown in Figure 4, errors caused by truncation gradually decrease as the output-token budget increases.
claims.claim_summary: As shown in Figure 4, errors caused by truncation gradually decrease as the output-token budget increases.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Notably, although the Primer is synthesized with a 32k maximum output-token budget, it continues to improve the Student at larger budgets, indicating that its knowledge and solution strategies are not tied to the specific output-token budget used during synthesis.
claims.claim_summary: Notably, although the Primer is synthesized with a 32k maximum output-token budget, it continues to improve the Student at larger budgets, indicating that its knowledge and solution strategies are not tied to the specific output-token budget used during synthesis.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: At the largest tested budget, APO approaches and even slightly underperforms the baseline, whereas UTT, although not reaching Teacher performance, remains between the baseline and the Teacher.
claims.claim_summary: At the largest tested budget, APO approaches and even slightly underperforms the baseline, whereas UTT, although not reaching Teacher performance, remains between the baseline and the Teacher.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: This suggests that explicit knowledge guidance derived from Teacher-Student interaction can narrow this gap more effectively than prompt optimization that primarily relies on iterative search guided by evaluation signals.
claims.claim_summary: This suggests that explicit knowledge guidance derived from Teacher-Student interaction can narrow this gap more effectively than prompt optimization that primarily relies on iterative search guided by evaluation signals.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: UTT completes Primer synthesis in 1.6 hours through 281 API model calls, approximately 0.68 million input tokens, and 5.57 million output tokens.
claims.claim_summary: UTT completes Primer synthesis in 1.6 hours through 281 API model calls, approximately 0.68 million input tokens, and 5.57 million output tokens.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Together with Table 3, these results show that UTT outperforms all KD baselines without parameter updates.
claims.claim_summary: Together with Table 3, these results show that UTT outperforms all KD baselines without parameter updates.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The full method improves over the Student without a Primer across all four knowledge-gap subsets.
claims.claim_summary: The full method improves over the Student without a Primer across all four knowledge-gap subsets.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Accuracy increases from 33.7%, 33.3%, 60.0%, and 0.0% to 65.3%, 56.0%, 72.5%, and 5.0% on the distillation-training, distillation-test, retention, and frontier subsets, respectively.
claims.claim_summary: Accuracy increases from 33.7%, 33.3%, 60.0%, and 0.0% to 65.3%, 56.0%, 72.5%, and 5.0% on the distillation-training, distillation-test, retention, and frontier subsets, respectively.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Compared with random selection, knowledge-gap selection improves distillation-training and distillation-test accuracy by 9.7 and 6.0 percentage points, respectively, maintains the same retention accuracy, and yields one additional correct response on the frontier subset.
claims.claim_summary: Compared with random selection, knowledge-gap selection improves distillation-training and distillation-test accuracy by 9.7 and 6.0 percentage points, respectively, maintains the same retention accuracy, and yields one additional correct response on the frontier subset.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: These results suggest that selecting synthesis problems according to the Teacher–Student knowledge gap provides more targeted teaching signals and a more consistent overall improvement.
claims.claim_summary: These results suggest that selecting synthesis problems according to the Teacher–Student knowledge gap provides more targeted teaching signals and a more consistent overall improvement.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Removing the Prompter yields the highest distillation-training accuracy of 72.4%, but reduces distillation-test and retention accuracy from 56.0% and 72.5% to 48.8% and 70.0%, respectively, while frontier accuracy remains at 5.0%.
claims.claim_summary: Removing the Prompter yields the highest distillation-training accuracy of 72.4%, but reduces distillation-test and retention accuracy from 56.0% and 72.5% to 48.8% and 70.0%, respectively, while frontier accuracy remains at 5.0%.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: This trade-off suggests that direct Teacher demonstrations fit the synthesis problems more strongly, whereas the Prompter helps transfer the acquired knowledge to problems not used for synthesis.
claims.claim_summary: This trade-off suggests that direct Teacher demonstrations fit the synthesis problems more strongly, whereas the Prompter helps transfer the acquired knowledge to problems not used for synthesis.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Without validation gating, distillation-training, distillation-test, and frontier accuracy decrease from 65.3%, 56.0%, and 5.0% to 59.2%, 39.3%, and 3.8%, respectively, while retention accuracy in- creases from 72.5% to 80.0%.
claims.claim_summary: Without validation gating, distillation-training, distillation-test, and frontier accuracy decrease from 65.3%, 56.0%, and 5.0% to 59.2%, 39.3%, and 3.8%, respectively, while retention accuracy in- creases from 72.5% to 80.0%.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Thus, removing the gate does not yield a consistent improvement, but instead trades lower accuracy on the other three subsets for higher retention accuracy.
claims.claim_summary: Thus, removing the gate does not yield a consistent improvement, but instead trades lower accuracy on the other three subsets for higher retention accuracy.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Among the three batch sizes, the default batch size of 16 performs best on the distillation-training and distillation-test subsets and ties batch size 32 on the retention and frontier subsets.
claims.claim_summary: Among the three batch sizes, the default batch size of 16 performs best on the distillation-training and distillation-test subsets and ties batch size 32 on the retention and frontier subsets.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The smaller batch size of 8 performs worse across all four subsets.
claims.claim_summary: The smaller batch size of 8 performs worse across all four subsets.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Although batch size 32 maintains the retention and frontier results, its distillation-training and distillation-test accuracy decreases to 59.2% and 45.2%, respectively.
claims.claim_summary: Although batch size 32 maintains the retention and frontier results, its distillation-training and distillation-test accuracy decreases to 59.2% and 45.2%, respectively.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: These results suggest that an intermediate batch size provides a better balance between the amount of teaching evidence consolidated in each update and the frequency of Primer refinement.
claims.claim_summary: These results suggest that an intermediate batch size provides a better balance between the amount of teaching evidence consolidated in each update and the frequency of Primer refinement.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The Primer improves both accuracy and Fast1 in all four settings.
claims.claim_summary: The Primer improves both accuracy and Fast1 in all four settings.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Although the gain mag- nitude varies across configurations, the same Primer remains effective without resynthesis under the evaluated changes to quantization and thinking mode.
claims.claim_summary: Although the gain mag- nitude varies across configurations, the same Primer remains effective without resynthesis under the evaluated changes to quantization and thinking mode.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: This example preserves the compact form produced by the Synthesizer and illustrates how problem-solving experience from different problems is consolidated into a textual Primer.
claims.claim_summary: This example preserves the compact form produced by the Synthesizer and illustrates how problem-solving experience from different problems is consolidated into a textual Primer.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The Primer in Example 2 emphasizes output-format compliance and the basic requirements for custom CUDA implementations, and summarizes extension binding, scan-style operators, lazy compilation, and common compilation and runtime errors.
claims.claim_summary: The Primer in Example 2 emphasizes output-format compliance and the basic requirements for custom CUDA implementations, and summarizes extension binding, scan-style operators, lazy compilation, and common compilation and runtime errors.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: This exam- ple illustrates how a Primer organizes code-generation requirements, implementation patterns, and engineering troubleshooting experience for CUDA operators into textual guidance that can be di- rectly used by the Student.
claims.claim_summary: This exam- ple illustrates how a Primer organizes code-generation requirements, implementation patterns, and engineering troubleshooting experience for CUDA operators into textual guidance that can be di- rectly used by the Student.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: This example illustrates how a Primer combines computational patterns, implementation details, and engineering experience to guide code generation and validation.
claims.claim_summary: This example illustrates how a Primer combines computational patterns, implementation details, and engineering experience to guide code generation and validation.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The Primer in Example 3 organizes figure interpretation, geometric reasoning, and answer output into a sequential problem-solving process.
claims.claim_summary: The Primer in Example 3 organizes figure interpretation, geometric reasoning, and answer output into a sequential problem-solving process.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: It guides the Student to associate numerical labels with geometric objects, distinguish easily confused concepts such as radius and diameter, and solve for the target quantity using tools such as angle propagation, similarity relations, and area decomposition.
claims.claim_summary: It guides the Student to associate numerical labels with geometric objects, distinguish easily confused concepts such as radius and diameter, and solve for the target quantity using tools such as angle propagation, similarity relations, and area decomposition.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: It also addresses repeated figure interpretation and reasoning budget exhaustion through strategies that limit alternative interpretations, focus on the target quantity, and ensure timely answer output, illustrating concrete forms of textual guidance for multimodal problem solving.
claims.claim_summary: It also addresses repeated figure interpretation and reasoning budget exhaustion through strategies that limit alternative interpretations, focus on the target quantity, and ensure timely answer output, illustrating concrete forms of textual guidance for multimodal problem solving.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Nearly every observed failure was identical: no final output — budget burned re-reading the figure, cataloguing every labeled value, or debating which vertex owns a number.
claims.claim_summary: Nearly every observed failure was identical: no final output — budget burned re-reading the figure, cataloguing every labeled value, or debating which vertex owns a number.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The primary goal of this work, however, is to provide a proof of concept that knowledge distillation of LLMs can occur in text form, with no weight updates required.
claims.claim_summary: The primary goal of this work, however, is to provide a proof of concept that knowledge distillation of LLMs can occur in text form, with no weight updates required.
